name: Prostamax
summary: A short lab-made peptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro) from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for prostate health; published evidence is limited to lab studies on cells and DNA.
what_it_is: Prostamax is a lab-made chain of four amino acids: lysine, glutamic acid, aspartic acid and proline (Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro, or KEDP). The US National Library of Medicine indexes it under that name, and it comes from Vladimir Khavinson's 'peptide bioregulator' research in Russia; online catalogs promote it for the prostate. Its developers propose that short peptides like this loosen tightly packed DNA and switch genes back on, but this has only been studied in lab dishes.

evidence.why: Only lab studies were found, on white blood cells from elderly people and on DNA in test tubes, all from the developer's group; no human trials were found.

status_us.label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
status_us.note: Prostamax is not an FDA-approved drug and appears on none of FDA's compounding lists (nominated substances, updated May 2026; safety-risk and withdrawn nominations, April 2026). FDA allows pharmacy compounding only from ingredients that are in an approved drug, meet a USP standard, or are on or under review for its bulk list.

benefits.claim: Reactivated ribosomal genes and loosened tightly packed chromatin in white blood cells from people aged 75 to 88, in lab dishes
Loosened a tightly packed region near the center of chromosome 1 in the same cells
Changed the stability of DNA in test-tube experiments, which its developers propose explains its effects on genes

risks.risk: Promoted for the prostate, but no human safety or effectiveness data were found
No FDA-approved or pharmacy-compounded version exists, so products may not contain the Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro peptide indexed under this name

avoid_if: Prostate cancer, or a raised PSA that a clinician has not yet assessed

before: General health check with a clinician
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for Prostamax; urinary or prostate symptoms deserve a standard medical evaluation in their own right.

studies.title: Effects of Short Peptides on Lymphocyte Chromatin in Senile Subjects
studies.people: White blood cells from people aged 75 to 88
studies.finding: Prostamax and four other short peptides reactivated ribosomal genes and loosened densely packed chromatin; Prostamax also loosened structural chromatin near the center of chromosome 1.

studies.title: Peptide Regulation of Gene Expression: A Systematic Review
studies.people: Cell cultures and DNA in test tubes
studies.finding: A review by the developers of evidence that short peptides bind DNA and change gene activity; KEDP altered the melting temperature and stability of DNA.

ask_your_clinician: Do my urinary or prostate symptoms need a PSA test or prostate exam first?

notes_for_editor: Identity is solid (NLM MeSH record C500342 maps Prostamax to H-Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro-OH). The only evidence opened is lab work on chromatin in white blood cells from elderly donors and DNA studies, all from the developer's group. Online catalogs cite a rat study of chronic aseptic prostatitis (reportedly Bulletin of Experimental Biology and Medicine, 2013) and a 2012 paper on Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro chromatin effects (PubMed 23221144); neither could be opened (PubMed pages failed to load and the shared web-search budget ran out), so no prostate benefit is claimed. Russian status not confirmed.
